thread:
mike: Heads-up — around 08:04 we saw ~40% of EU customer traffic get routed to us-west for Model-v2 when eu pool returned 503s. Not a full outage but obvious cross-region spill.
anya: saw it too in the dashboard, latency spiked for enterprise tier customers. console shows fallback to v2-us as default variant.
leah: does the routing policy explicitly allow cross-region fallback for enterprise? I thought enterprise was pinned to eu-first.
jamal: default policy: region -> tier -> variant. Fallback chain should be region-local variant then tier-compatible remote. But telemetry shows multiple hops.
sre-bot: auto-detect: increased multi-hop-fallback rate 08:04-08:12, threshold breached. Alert mailed to #oncall.
mike: logs indicate quota-gate triggered on eu-prod-gpu pool at 08:03, then our redispatch picks candidate in us-west. But token-quota for that variant was near-cap too. Guess we bounced again.
anya: exact symptom: user requests go eu -> try eu-v2 -> 503 -> fallback to eu-v1 (compatible) but eu-v1 full -> fallback to us-west-v2. Some tenants configured variant-strict but will still allow remote fallback?
leah: that sounds like two problems: 1) fallback order includes cross-region before exhausting all local variants, 2) no circuit breaker to prevent bounce back-and-forth.
jamal: agreed. Also our metric 'fallback_hops' is 0/1/2 but we never surface it on the console or use it in policy checks.
mike: paste of the routing snippet we used (simplified):
```json
{"route_policies": [{"priority": 10, "selector": "region:eu, tier:enterprise", "fallback_order": ["eu-v2","eu-v1","us-west-v2"], "allow_cross_region": true, "max_hops": 3}]}
```
anya: note: max_hops=3 doesn't prevent oscillation if remote variant later routes back to eu during repair window. we saw a case where us-west then hit eu-prefixed fallback because of topology reconciling.
leah: we need a safety net: add hop-aware cooldown per request-id or per-tenant to prevent immediate multi-hop. also add a 'preferred_region_fallback_only' flag for customers who opt-in.
jamal: temporary hotfix proposal: change fallback_order to exhaust all local variants and only then try remote, and set allow_cross_region=false for enterprise tier until we patch.
mike: operational ask: can we push hotfix to policy service now? deploy-bot: queued patch to canary at 08:30, will target policy config and a small runtime change.
deploy-bot: patch: update policy for selector region:eu,tier:enterprise -> allow_cross_region=false; add metric fallback_hop_count tagged by tenant; rollout 5% -> 50% -> 100% over 10m.
anya: also add alerting: if fraction of requests with hop_count>=2 exceeds 0.5% in 5m, page oncall.
leah: long-term: UI change — console should show the effective fallback graph for each route with real-time hop histogram and a toggle to disable cross-region fallback per tenant. Makes support debugging way faster.
jamal: and we should implement a per-tenant circuit-breaker: after N cross-region fallbacks in T seconds, mark tenant as 'no-remote-fallback' for cooldown period.
mike: agreed. Also add telemetry for 'fallback_chain' sample traces (store only 1% for privacy).
anya: after the canary rollout, we'll monitor: key metrics to watch — latency_p50/p95 for enterprise eu tenants, fallback_hop_rate, cross_region_traffic_ratio, and grpc 503 rate on eu pool.
leah: FYI I added a quick patch to the routing-service simulator to reproduce the bounce. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/routingservice/pulls/482 (small change to fallback logic + unit tests).
mike: thanks. timeline?
jamal: canary at 08:30, 50% by 08:40, full by 08:50 if no regression. I'll keep manual hold if hop_rate > 0.2%.
anya: oncall — please watch for tenant-visible errors and customer slack. I'll prepare a short internal note for CS.
leah: postmortem action items: 1) expose fallback_hop metric in console, 2) default policy change to prefer local variants, 3) implement per-tenant cooldown circuit breaker, 4) add UI toggle and shortcut to disable cross-region fallback, 5) sample traces for fallback chains.
mike: scoreboard: hotfix live on canary. tagging @support-team and @account-ops so they're aware. :thumbsup:
support-team: acknowledged. I'll standby for customer reports.
deploy-bot: rollout progressed to 50% at 08:35.
sre-bot: multi-hop fallback rate dropped from 1.1% -> 0.15% during canary. No paging thresholds hit.
jamal: rolling to 100% now.
mike: great, let's keep this thread for notes and attach postmortem once we confirm final metrics.
leah: I'll start writing the postmortem draft and include the simulation logs and console mockups.
anya: thanks all.
